stem: A radar has a power of 10 kW and is operating at a frequency of 20 GHz. It is located on the top of a hill of height 500 m. Calculate the maximum distance upto which it can detect object located on the surface of the Earth. (Radius of Earth = \( 6.4 \times 10^{6} \) m)
solution:
Maximum distance (range) \( = \)
\( d = \sqrt{2Rh} \)
\( = \sqrt{2 \times (6.4 \times 10^{6}) \times 500}\ \text{m} \)
\( = 8 \times 10^{4} = 80\ \text{km} \),
where \( R \) is radius of the Earth and \( h \) is the height of the radar above Earth's surface.
_note: The stated power (10 kW) and frequency (20 GHz) are not used and are not needed — the range depends only on R and h. The book's own solution uses neither. Transcribed as printed.

stem: If the height of a TV transmitting antenna is 128 m, how much square area can be covered by the transmitted signal if the receiving antenna is at the ground level? (Radius of the Earth = 6400 km)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the substitution line prints \(3.14 \times (40)^{2}\), which evaluates to \(5024\), while the very next line prints \(5144.58\) — the CORRECT value, which follows from \(d^{2} = 2Rh = 1638.4\) km\(^{2}\) rather than from a distance rounded to 40. The example's final answer is right; only the substitution was rounded. The same line also sets the unit as "k4m\(^{2}\)", a garbled km\(^{2}\), confirmed on the printed page rather than inferred from the text layer.]

Range \( = d = \sqrt{2Rh} \)
\( = \sqrt{2(6400 \times 10^{3})(128)} \)
\( = \sqrt{16.384 \times 10^{5} \times 10^{3}} \)
\( = \sqrt{16.384 \times 10^{8}} \)
\( = 4.047 \times 10^{4} \)
\( = 40.470\ \text{km} \)
Area covered \( = \pi d^{2} = 3.14 \times (40)^{2} \)
\( = 5144.58\ \text{k4m}^{2} \)
_note: TWO printed defects, both transcribed as printed rather than repaired. (1) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY in the last two lines: the substitution 3.14 x (40)^2 evaluates to 5024, not the 5144.58 the book prints. The printed value 5144.58 is the CORRECT one and follows from d^2 = 2Rh = 1638.4 km^2 (3.14 x 1638.4 = 5144.58); the book rounded d to 40 in the substitution line only. (2) The unit is printed as 'k4m^2' — a garbled 'km^2' (verified on the rendered page at 9x zoom, it really is set as k4m2). The final answer 5144.58 km^2 is right; only the substitution line and the unit are wrong. Candidate for apply-solved-fixes.ts + an errata bracket.

stem: The height of a transmitting antenna is 68 m and the receiving antenna is at the top of a tower of height 34 m. Calculate the maximum distance between them for satisfactory transmission in line of sight mode. (radius of Earth = 6400 km)
